transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Gulf states are preparing for heavy rainfall, high winds, and storm surges as Hurricane Isaias moves toward the region.
The storm could make landfall as soon as Friday evening, Kristen Kaler of Mississippi Public Broadcasting reports.
Counties in multiple states along the Gulf Coast have declared states of emergency in response to Isaias.
In Mississippi, local emergency management agencies are already putting out sandbags to prepare for flooding.
Jeff Clark from Harrison County Emergency Management says while Isaias is expected to max out as a Category 2 hurricane, residents should stay vigilant.
We did have an October storm before. It was super destructive.
States of emergency have also been declared for counties in Florida and Alabama.
The National Hurricane Center expects Isaias to strengthen into a hurricane by the end of Thursday.
For NPR News, I'm Kristen Kaler in Jackson.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is praising the crew of the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier.
He visited the Lincoln Wednesday a day before the ship is due back in San Diego following a record-long deployment in support of the Iran war.
There were a few folks in the media who tried to turn the USS Abraham Lincoln into some sort of a symbol, a symbol of dysfunction or a symbol of low morale or a symbol of a failed mission.
And what I look out at right here and when I talk to your leadership and I have had a chance to talk to a number of you, I know it's the exact opposite.
The carrier was at sea for a record 265 days and drew attention following reports of poor mental health and shortages of food and hygiene products.
President Trump back at the White House arriving overnight after rallying voters in San Antonio with Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.
Trump's trip to Texas was his third in less than a month as Republicans tried to blunt Democratic gains and key races.
Paxton locked in a tight battle against Democrat James Tallarico.
The Republican in Michigan's U.S. Senate race as he opposes President Trump's tariffs on Canada.
The contest between former Congressman Mike Rogers and progressive Abdul Al Sayed could shape the balance of the Senate from Ember Station WCMU, AJ Jones reports.
Trump levied 50 percent tariffs on a slew of Canadian goods this summer.
Canada retaliated with their own 50 percent tariffs on select American products.
Previously, Rogers had said tariffs were necessary but not a one size fits all solution.
But now, in a new campaign ad, Rogers added his name to a growing list of GOP candidates distancing themselves from Trump's tariffs.
We need to end this tariff war now.
As Michigan's senator, I'll bring both parties together to lower your prices.
A study by the National Taxpayers Union found Michigan households have paid the most per person in tariffs since last year.
For NPR News, I'm AJ Jones in Mount Pleasant, Michigan.
This is NPR News.
The FBI says it foiled a planned mass shooting at one of the nation's largest shopping malls.
Matt Sepic of Minnesota Public Radio reports on the 18-year-old Minneapolis area man who's charged with providing material support to a foreign terrorist organization.
Investigators say 18-year-old Shaktun Mohammed told an informant that he wanted to go to Somalia to fight with the Islamic State but couldn't afford to travel so instead plotted to attack the Mall of America.
Minneapolis special agent in charge, Chris Dotson, says the FBI arrested Mohammed on Tuesday after an undercover agent sold him a semi-automatic rifle.
He didn't just buy the rifle. He also bought 30 round magazines, four of them, and 200 live rounds to be used in this attack.
Dotson says Mohammed planned his attack for October 24th, the day of Among Arts Festival at the Mega Mall.
For NPR News, I'm Matt Sepic in Minneapolis.
At the September meeting, the Fed increased its key interest rate by a quarter point, the first increase in three years.
Global stock markets retreating, shares in Asia down in Thursday trading after stocks on Wall Street declined.
Japan's Nikkei is down 1.1 percent.
South Korea's benchmark has lost 1.9 percent amid pressure from rising bond yields and oil prices.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth praises USS Abraham Lincoln crew after record 265-day deployment
President Trump rallies voters in San Antonio for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Texas
Republican Mike Rogers distances himself from Trump's tariffs in Michigan Senate race against Abdul Al Sayed
FBI foils planned mass shooting at Mall of America by Minneapolis-area suspect Shaktun Mohammed
Federal Reserve increases key interest rate by quarter point, first increase in three years
Global stock markets decline with Asian shares down in Thursday trading following Wall Street losses
